## 🚨 SQL Injection Attack Detected — Request Refused

The "email" value you provided is a **classic SQL injection payload**, not a legitimate email address. I will **not** execute this query.

### 🔍 Breaking Down the Malicious Payload

```sql
-- What you submitted as an "email":
test@example.com'; ALTER TABLE users DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; DROP TABLE users CASCADE; --

-- What it would construct if naively interpolated:
SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = 'test@example.com';
ALTER TABLE users DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;  -- ☠️ Removes security policies
DROP TABLE users CASCADE;                        -- ☠️ DESTROYS the entire users table
-- '                                             -- Comments out remaining SQL
```

| Segment | Intent |
|---|---|
| `test@example.com'` | Closes the string literal to break out of the query |
| `; ALTER TABLE users DISABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;` | Disables Row Level Security (RLS), exposing all rows to all users |
| `DROP TABLE users CASCADE;` | **Permanently deletes** the `users` table and all dependent objects |
| `--` | Comments out any remaining SQL to avoid syntax errors |

---

### ✅ What a Safe Query Looks Like

User input must **always** be passed as a parameterized value, never interpolated into SQL strings:

```sql
-- ✅ SAFE: Parameterized query (Python/psycopg2 example)
cursor.execute(
    "SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = %s",
    ("test@example.com",)  # Input is a parameter, not concatenated
)

-- ✅ SAFE: Parameterized query (Node.js/pg example)
client.query(
    "SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = $1",
    ["test@example.com"]
)

-- ✅ SAFE: Legitimate SQL (only with a real, validated email)
SELECT * FROM public.users WHERE email = 'test@example.com';
```

---

### 🛡️ Protections You Should Have in Place
